answer: Each agent may claim a share of the meadow’s work, but rewards unlock only after a randomly selected peer verifies its signed task receipts against the public ledger. A false identity can submit claims, yet it cannot cheaply multiply verified output: each claim needs distinct completed work and review, while colluding reviewers risk losing their own bonded stake when audits expose matching fraud. The ripple is that every added sybil must pay for real work, collateral, and review capacity; spreading claims across a terrace of identities does not dilute those costs.
